note: Contrarian Shark, skeptical-researcher angle. Judged only against the locked North Star surfaces, not the elegance table’s attempt to reopen them. Wave bodies specify the (B) lab; the HOLD table still spends zero until (B) is “ratified.” That is one plan with two incompatible treatments. Heartbeat at `heartbeat.json`.

findings.section: Wave 3 intent vs W3.1 HOLD / elegance pass
findings.criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview (cwd = project folder, OS-assigned port never 8777, own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped)
findings.message: The locked criterion is the per-project lab. Wave 3’s own Intent says that locked line “IS option (B) … so the manager is built.” The elegance table then HOLDs W3.1 and every dependent (ensure/probe/reap, fake_lab, labs endpoints, boot reap, healthcheck walk, `rnd labs`, Lab chip) until John picks (A) jupyter-serve or (B) a new lab, and orders “spend zero” until (B). Those two sentences cannot both be the build contract. (A) is not criterion 1: not per-project, not cwd = the project folder, not an OS-assigned port, not registered/listed/stoppable/reaped like a preview. A Foreman that honors HOLDs ships no lab. A Foreman that honors wave text builds a manager the table forbids. Criterion 1 is not a measurement you can take until the independent variable (which process is “the project’s own JupyterLab”) is fixed to one treatment.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file (starting the lab if needed)
findings.message: Kind-dispatch is KEEP’d; the Location it 302s to is HOLD’d. If HOLDs win, `/notebook` exists and has nowhere to send the browser. If (B) is built, the click goes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab/tree/…` of a lab W3.1 is not allowed to spawn. If (A) is wired instead, `/lab/tree/<rel>` is relative to jupyter-serve’s root, not the project folder, so an in-effort notebook is a 404 or the wrong tree — and nothing starts or restarts a dead lab. Criterion 2 is one click that lands on that file in that project’s lab. This route, as HOLD’d, has no such target. W5.1 KEEP of the path is not a substitute for a destination.

findings.section: Wave 5 — dispatch vs W5.3 HOLD (interstitial / lab_ready)
findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.message: The same wave requires `'lab' -> lab_server.ensure_lab -> 302` and, in the next sentence, that a cold lab “answers immediately” via a poll page whose start is backgrounded. W3.2’s `ensure_lab` still waits `health_timeout=20`. Those are two control flows; the plan does not name which thread starts the process. W5.3 then HOLDs both the interstitial and `lab_ready` until a recorded click is blank or hung under a blocking 302. Criterion 2 forbids that blank page; using the forbidden outcome as the trigger to build the mitigation is how the failure ships. What remains is 302-after-probe. A cold JupyterLab boot is then a silent tab — connection-refused or a spinnerless wait — which the wave’s own Intent already admits is a blank page. `fake_lab` answers at once, so W3–W7 never see a real boot; W8 is the first clocked start, after the mechanism is parked.

findings.topic: sign-off does not observe the opens
findings.criterion: 5 — on a real project a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected, a short .py opens as a notebook, a long .py opens in the editor, a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: The six screenshots do not measure the four locked claims. (a) “file selected” is a document title containing the basename; `fake_lab` is specified to serve exactly `<title><basename></title>` for `/lab/tree/<rel>`, so the stub teaches the gate a tautology, and a real JupyterLab shell with the path only in the URL can pass. (c) is “eyes-on” that VS Code has the file, while the automated assert is a `vscode://file/` href — not `code -r`. (d) allows the fixture URL to be the pre-existing tailnet jupyter-serve at `:8446` “or” the managed lab; a green `04-live-link.png` then does not corroborate that a project lab came up. That is a confound: the live-link treatment can be the old server while criteria 1–2 still fail. Criterion 5 is eyes on the opens on the surface he uses, not URL-shape lints plus a PNG of an interstitial.

findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`), and the row says which
findings.message: The locked launcher is `code -r <file>`. The editor page still dual-fires `ANCHOR_EDITOR_CMD` and `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)`, which can open the file twice and put an absolute path in page history. W5.4 HOLDs the URI half “until a recorded click where `code -r` did not land,” while W5’s deliverable and W8’s pass condition still require a `vscode://file/` href and capture that navigation. The live gate is wired to the parked half. Remote `vscode://` on a tablet is the parked non-goal (iPad editing). Criterion 3 is satisfied by a non-blocking `code -r` that actually raises the file. Prove that seam; do not gate on the scheme the HOLD forbids.

findings.section: Wave 2 — W2.1 HOLD / Wave 2 GWT / Wave 8 live-link fixture
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, or this machine's tailnet name renders as a link; every other host stays text
findings.message: Production resolution of “this machine’s tailnet name” after the W2.1 HOLD is `localhost` + `127.0.0.1` + `socket.gethostname()` (this host’s friendly name is not guaranteed to be the tailnet name) plus an optional `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. The auto-probe that would have read `Self.DNSName` is parked; `tests/fake_tailscale.py` is not earned. The wave’s own Given/When/Then still requires `ANCHOR_TAILSCALE_CMD` pointing at that stub and the stub’s DNSName to return a URL — an acceptance test of a HOLD’d path. Sign-off injects `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES` and then confirms the override, which is not evidence the NSSM `anchor` service knows the FQDN on a boot where the env is unset. Journal 0110’s URL is that FQDN. Criterion 4 is a row John can click without a test-only env, not a stubbed frozenset.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens at /lab/tree/<rel>
findings.message: Files-tile clicks are `window.open` of `/notebook` with `dir=''` on the claim that “the path is project-relative there.” The plan does not show that the files payload actually carries project-root-relative paths. The register already has `dir` because effort-relative paths are a real case. If a produced file is effort-relative, `dir=''` joins to a path that fails containment or 404s, and the files tile is the one named surface that never starts the lab on the right file. No Given/When/Then uses a files-tile row; the JS is asserted textually. Criterion 2 names that tile. Register and plan inherit `dir`; files are specified as if they do not need it, without a proof that the producer agrees.

findings.topic: mixed Where cell url vs path
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / tailnet URL renders as a link (new window)
findings.message: The parser says a cell carrying both a path and a URL “keeps the path as the open target.” The renderer’s first branch is `if (it.url)` → `<a href=it.url>`. Those cannot both be true of the same row. If `url` is set, the live link wins and the path is dead. If `url` is withheld whenever a path is present, the journal-0110 workaround rows (`RUN-*.html` launch pages whose Where cell also mentions the tailnet address) stay path-opens and criterion 4 does not fire on the rows that motivated it. The plan never says which encoding existing registers use, and never migrates them. A construct that is specified two ways is untestable: W6’s fixture rows are pure URL or pure path, so the mixed case — the actual 0110 shape — is never observed.

The locked labels are notebook and editor. The chip also prints `lab` for `.ipynb`. That is a third word the criterion does not use, so a notebook row does not “say which” in the vocabulary the surface locked. Harmless if renamed; as specified it fails the letter of criterion 3 on the most common row.

findings.section: plan header test-command vs Wave 8 gate
findings.criterion: 5 — seen on the page before it ships … Playwright screenshots, then the release pipeline
findings.message: The machine-countable `test-command` is three files (`test_code_windows_2026_09_07.py`, `test_steward_deliverables.py`, `test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`). W8’s “nets green” bar is the full suite plus per-wave stub gates plus Playwright sign-off. If Foreman runs the header command, W0/W1b/W2/W3/W4 stub files and `test_code_opens_signoff_w4.py` never have to pass. Criterion 5 is the page, then the pipeline; a gate that cannot see the sign-off is not that criterion. Name one command that actually counts the surfaces you claim, or admit the header command is a lint.
